The general rule is role exclusivity: a repository path named in a sentence has exactly one role, so any path already bound to another input key is not also a member of a *_paths list. challenger_routes.why_considered: A goal of the form 'Write the text T to the file X and save the report to Y' returned status PASS__COMPOSED_CAPABILITY_CHAIN with pass=True after writing those 11 bytes into Y. X, the file the goal actually named, was never created on disk and the front door reported the goal done. Composition is attempted at exactly the two moments where the primary path has already failed, and both call sites returned the chain's own verdict untouched. The gate that catches this, promised_artifact_errors, had already run; its result was discarded.
challenger_routes.why_not_selected_or_selected: SELECTED: apply the gate that already exists to the fallback before it may report success. Two supporting defects were found by measuring the same family. (1) Template key order for the repair capabilities is output_path, source_root, test_argv, test_paths, and test_argv is derived FROM the test paths, so counting a derived argv as a competing claim cancelled the role against itself: exclusivity emptied a correct test_paths, the fallback then assigned every file in the sentence, source included. (2) That masking hid a second defect: _repo_paths only checks that a path RESOLVES under the root, so 'test command /usr/bin/python3 T' bound usr/bin/python3 as a test file and the adapter rejected it with FILE_INVALID. Both are fixed generally: an argv is not a claim, and a role list may only name files that exist. Measured: the false PASS becomes FAIL_CLOSED__PROMISED_ARTIFACT_MISSING naming the exact missing file; test_paths on the route-admission sentence returns exactly the named test; test_paths on the strict-progress sentence returns exactly the named test with no interpreter. BROAD_WEB_OR_COMMUNITY: https://api.github.com/search/repositories?q=postcondition%20verify%20effect%20not%20rerun -- a mutating command is verified by the state it left, never by running it twice; no standalone project owns the rule because it is a property of the check
